title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 203
paragraphs: In addition to these, the Opuntian Locrians had been summoned to come in their full force, along with a thousand of the Phokians: for the Greeks themselves had sent word to them, saying through messengers that they had come as forerunners of the others, that the rest of the allies were expected any day, that their sea was safely guarded — watched by the Athenians and the Aeginetans and those appointed to serve in the fleet — and that they had nothing to fear. For it was no god, they said, who was coming to attack Greece, but a man; and no mortal was born, nor would be, without some evil mingled into his fortunes at birth, with the greatest evils befalling the greatest men. The one marching against them, being mortal, would therefore be destined to fail in his expectations. Hearing this, they came to help the others at Trachis.
